drafts.prompt: Name a Linux kernel config option
drafts.accepts: Any CONFIG_ symbol that is defined in a Kconfig file in the Linux kernel source tree.
Any named kernel thread that appears as a kernel process in the Linux kernel source or in ps output.

drafts.prompt: Name a Linux network interface type
drafts.accepts: Any link type accepted by iproute2's ip link add command or listed in its link-type documentation.
Any event name listed by perf list, including generic hardware, cache, software and tracepoint events.
Any dotted tunable name that appears under /proc/sys and is documented in the kernel Documentation/admin-guide or sysctl.conf references.
Any LC_ constant defined in Apple's mach-o/loader.h for Mach-O binaries.
Any named model that specifies the allowed orderings of memory reads and writes across processors or replicas, from hardware, language or distributed-systems literature.
Any named software that collects metrics or checks the health of hosts or services and alerts on them, open-source or commercial.
Any named communication protocol specified in an RFC, IEEE, ITU or vendor standard, or a documented historic protocol.
Any admin or I/O command opcode defined in the NVMe base specification or its command-set specifications, such as the NVM or Zoned Namespace command sets.
Any named protocol that exchanges routing information to build forwarding tables, wired, wireless, mesh or historic.
Any AF_ constant defined in the Linux or BSD socket headers for a socket domain.
Any setting name documented in systemd.exec, systemd.service, systemd.unit or related systemd.* manual pages for unit files.
Any extension name in the IANA TLS ExtensionType registry.
Any named background service program on a Unix-like system, as named in its man page or the system's standard service list.
Any named command interpreter that runs scripts or interactive sessions on a Unix-like system, including historic and niche shells.
Any signal name defined in signal.h or signal(7) on a Unix-like system, including platform-specific and real-time signals.
Any named X11 or Wayland program that manages window placement and decoration, tiling or floating, including historic ones.

drafts.prompt: Name a Windows kernel object type
drafts.accepts: Any named object type registered with the Windows NT Object Manager, as listed by tools such as WinObj or documented in Windows internals references.
